sections.overview: Satin Beauty is a geometrid moth of European woodland; French sources call it Boarmie du Sapin.
sections.identification: Adults have a 30–40 mm wingspan and mottled brown forewings that can fade with wear.
sections.habitat: It occurs in deciduous and coniferous woodland, with larvae using several conifer and broadleaf food plants.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed mainly on conifers such as spruce, fir and yew.
sections.behavior: Adults fly in one generation, chiefly from late June to early August, and come to light.
sections.reproduction: The larva overwinters young on its food plant and later pupates in loose soil.
sections.ecology: It can be confused with Alcis repandata, but differences in wing pattern and genitalia aid identification.
sections.conservation: It is locally Near Threatened in Flanders and rare in parts of Belgium; this is a regional assessment, not a global status.
